solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Water fern sick wife found in dockland area

indicators.note: found in says these pieces are placed inside the dockland word

parts.note: a port is a harbour area with docks

explanation.surface: An unwell wife discovered somewhere around the docks, with a water fern thrown in.
explanation.definitionFit: Pillwort is a small aquatic fern of ponds and lake margins, so a botanical example of a water fern.

clue.text: Woman taking step to identify plains

explanation.surface: A woman takes a step towards identifying a stretch of flat country.
explanation.walkthrough: PAS is the French word for step, familiar from ballet (pas de deux); the pampas are the grassy plains of South America.
explanation.definitionFit: The pampas are the vast treeless plains of Argentina, so 'plains' is a straight synonym.

clue.text: Article in seagoing vessel having one dimension

indicators.note: the article sits inside the vessel

parts.note: an ocean liner; it goes round the article

explanation.surface: A newspaper article about some ship, which apparently has only one dimension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' reads as a piece of writing in the surface; here it is the grammatical article A.
explanation.definitionFit: Something linear extends along a line only, which is to say it has one dimension.

clue.text: Sport, one not a little tedious

parts.note: to sport a hat is to wear it
some = a fair amount, not a little

explanation.surface: Someone finds a particular sport more than a little tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sport' looks like a noun naming a game, but it is the verb meaning to wear or show off.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearisome means tiring through dullness, the same as tedious.

clue.text: Further tweaking involving impartial fellows badly rated externally

indicators.note: the letters of RATED are put together badly, i.e. rearranged

parts.note: RATED rearranged, split READ…T around the middle

explanation.surface: More fiddling with the rules, because some fair-minded men were poorly rated from outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' is only a link here. 'badly rated externally' asks for a short anagram used as the outer shell, which is easy to miss.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to readjust is to adjust again, and tweaking is small adjustment.

clue.text: Item left in car with sloping back

indicators.note: 'in' in its plain sense of inside

parts.note: a coupé is a two-door car with a sloping rear

explanation.surface: Something has been left behind in a fastback car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Item' is slang for a romantic couple (they're an item), not an object left in a car.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people who are 'an item' are a couple, so Item can stand for COUPLE.

clue.text: Asian bloke arrested by call to attention

indicators.note: the bloke is held inside the call

parts.note: oi! = a shout to get attention; it holds MAN

explanation.surface: A police scene: an Asian man is arrested after someone shouts at him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Asian' looks like it describes the bloke, but it is the definition on its own; OI is British slang for 'hey!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Oman is in Asia, on the Arabian Peninsula, so an Omani is an Asian.

clue.text: Pitiful way it turns up in City district

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the postcode letters

parts.note: EC is the postcode district of the City of London

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the word it is read from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: A sorry route through the City is the picture, with something turning up in a London district.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the City of London postcode; 'turns up' sends IT backwards to TI, which goes 'in' EC.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitiful and pathetic are synonyms for something arousing pity or contempt.

clue.text: Service, say, involving archdeacon and offspring

indicators.note: 'say' takes in the archdeacon and the offspring

parts.note: e.g. = for example, 'say'; it wraps the rest

explanation.surface: A church service with an archdeacon and some child taking part.
explanation.walkthrough: The Church of England styles an archdeacon 'the Venerable', abbreviated Ven.; 'say' is the example-giver EG.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Anglican evening prayer is one kind of church service.

clue.text: Male US attorney with place in a Buddhist centre

explanation.surface: An American lawyer with a place at a Buddhist centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' just strings the pieces together; 'in' joins the wordplay to the definition. Mandalay in Myanmar is a major centre of Buddhism.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandalay, the old royal capital of Burma, is full of monasteries and pagodas, a Buddhist centre.

clue.text: Man on board thrown by deals regularly backfiring

parts.note: cast means thrown, as a stone is cast

indicators.note: backfiring means the letters chosen are turned to run backwards
regularly means taking every other letter of deals

explanation.surface: A card player's deals keep going wrong, so the cards get thrown down.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of 'deals' give EL, which 'backfiring' turns to LE.
explanation.definitionFit: A castle, or rook, is one of the chess pieces, and 'man' is a usual word for a piece on a board.

clue.text: Old fish market's scandal over presentation of accounts?

parts.note: billing = sending out accounts to customers

explanation.surface: An old fish market caught up in a scandal about how its accounts were presented.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reads as 'about': the answer is a scandal about billings, a billings-gate. Billingsgate was London's historic fish market.
explanation.definitionFit: Billingsgate was the City of London's fish market for centuries before moving to Docklands.

clue.text: He made violins in the morning, very early!

parts.note: at 1 = at one o'clock, very early in the morning; 1 reads as I

explanation.surface: A violin maker who was at work first thing in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: One o'clock in the morning is 'very early'; the digit 1 is written as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amati family of Cremona were celebrated violin makers of the 16th and 17th centuries.

clue.text: Succulence mostly just in ices somehow

indicators.note: the letters are arranged somehow, i.e. mixed up
'mostly' cuts a letter off

explanation.surface: Juiciness, it seems, is found mostly in ices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link placing the succulence inside the ices, but it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Succulence is juiciness, the quality of being full of juice.

clue.text: Study post covering extremely useful discussion

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart

indicators.note: covering says the post word wraps around the letters from useful

parts.note: a station is a post where someone is placed on duty

indicators.note: extremely means the outermost letters, the two ends of useful

explanation.surface: A study post that covers something very useful, perhaps a job advert.
explanation.definitionFit: A consultation is a meeting held to talk something over, so it is a discussion.

clue.text: Pa's a rogue, appalling the High Court?

indicators.note: the letters are in an appalling state, i.e. jumbled

explanation.surface: Father is a scoundrel, which scandalises the court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appalling' reads as an adjective describing the rogue, but it is the anagram indicator. The question mark flags the High Court as ancient Athenian.
explanation.definitionFit: The Areopagus was the highest judicial council of ancient Athens, named after the hill where it sat.

clue.text: Southern explorer in charge of vessels finally going north — cutters

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means the pieces are read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: James Clark Ross was a British polar explorer

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of vessels

explanation.surface: An Antarctic explorer leads his ships north, with cutters as a naval vessel name.
explanation.walkthrough: Read upwards in the grid, S, ROSS, IC and S become the answer. 'cutters' looks like boats beside 'vessels', but it means a cutting tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Scissors are a cutting tool with two blades, so a pair are cutters.

clue.text: Arrogant fool with high-class china

explanation.surface: An arrogant fool shows off expensive porcelain.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class comes from Nancy Mitford's U and non-U language; 'china' is porcelain, not the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Assuming, as an adjective, means presumptuous or arrogant.

clue.text: Street trader's period plugging a type of eel containing bone

indicators.note: plugging means the period word fills a gap in the eel word
containing means the eel word holds the bone word as well

parts.note: the conger is a large sea eel
os is the Latin and anatomical word for bone
a term is a period of time

explanation.surface: A fishmonger's season selling conger eels with the bones still in.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'. OS and TERM go together inside CONGER, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A costermonger is a British street seller of fruit and vegetables from a barrow.

clue.text: Beam, seeing part of Carousel in telecast

indicators.note: the answer is part of the following words

explanation.surface: A spotlight picks out a scene from the musical Carousel on television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beam' suggests a light beam in a TV studio; it is a structural beam.
explanation.definitionFit: A lintel is the horizontal beam over a door or window.

clue.text: Mole crossing railway line with agility

indicators.note: crossing means the spy word lies across, so around, the railway letters

parts.note: a mole is a spy planted inside an organisation

explanation.surface: A burrowing mole nimbly crossing a railway track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mole' looks like the animal, but it is an undercover agent.
explanation.definitionFit: Spryly is an adverb meaning nimbly or energetically, which is acting with agility.

clue.text: Thus act, so to speak, getting sweet wine

indicators.note: said out loud, the words make the answer

parts.note: so = thus, turn = an act on stage

explanation.surface: Performing like this, one earns some sweet wine.
explanation.walkthrough: A turn is a short act in variety theatre; Sauternes is pronounced roughly 'so-TURN'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauternes is a sweet white dessert wine from Bordeaux.

clue.text: Husbandless woman in compound

indicators.note: the woman's name without H, husband

explanation.surface: A woman without a husband living in a walled compound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compound' looks like an enclosure where she lives; it is a chemical compound. H is the standard abbreviation for husband.
explanation.definitionFit: An ester is a chemical compound formed from an acid and an alcohol.

clue.text: Prudish people principally dress in fine clothes

indicators.note: only the principal, first letter of 'people'

explanation.surface: Prudish people above all like to dress in their finery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prudish people' reads as one phrase, but it splits: the adjective gives PRIM and 'people' only its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To primp is to dress or groom yourself carefully and smartly.

clue.text: Old rover loses right to supply narcotic drug

indicators.note: loses means the letter for right drops out of the word for the rover

parts.note: a rover is a sea rover, a pirate

explanation.surface: An elderly wanderer loses his right to deal narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: O + PIRATE without its R.
explanation.definitionFit: An opiate is a drug derived from opium, such as morphine, used as a narcotic painkiller.

clue.text: Gizmos daughters obtain in Indiana port

indicators.note: in places these pieces inside the port name

parts.note: Gary is a port city on Lake Michigan in Indiana
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Daughters buying gadgets in an American lakeside town.
explanation.definitionFit: Gadgetry is a collective term for gadgets, and gizmos are gadgets.

clue.text: Retired American chap exuding sweetness

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so US is turned round

explanation.surface: A retired American man with a charmingly sweet manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired American chap' looks like one old man; it splits into reversed US and a chap's name, the same Gary as the port in 25 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugary means sweet, or cloyingly sweet in manner, exuding sweetness.

clue.text: With support large Yankee becomes sly and treacherous

parts.note: Yankee is Y in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A big American, once he has backing, turns sly and treacherous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yankee' suggests an American; it is the radio code word for Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Weaselly means like a weasel: sly, shifty and untrustworthy.
